rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage neighborhood-building mass: one dominant compact bar-like volume, split/stepped into interlocking parts with a legible central void and a visible ground response to the access edge. It is not perfect—some surfaces still feel boxy and the section is relatively shallow—but the four views agree on the same organizational idea, and the void/threshold logic is present rather than decorative. The mass responds to the parcel without merely filling the boundary, and the blue frontage is answered by an accessible seam/undercut rather than a sealed edge. Program-wise, it plausibly supports compact mixed neighborhood living because it preserves active ground, hierarchy, and a public opening. The silhouette is more fragmented than ideal, but still continuous enough to pass as a single massing rule.
